meta.description: Assigns cause-effect nodes to packages based on essential nature. Torah LM2/27 contains zero bechina edges and zero pre-existing packages. All 3 edges are eitza (cause-effect). Nodes are grouped into new packages based on their essential thematic nature and polarity.

new_packages.rationale: Both nodes share the same essential nature: the act of looking carefully at each person and distributing burdens equitably. Node 1 describes the leader who does this (the parnas/manhig who leads with integrity), and node 3 describes the act itself (looking to assess each person properly). They are the same concept from two angles — the agent and the action. Moshe Rabbeinu is the paradigmatic example of both.

new_packages.rationale: This is a singleton node representing the distinct spiritual mechanism of hatarat nedarim (annulment of vows). Its essential nature is the release from binding obligations — a juridical-spiritual concept distinct from both the leadership that causes it and the salvation from sin that follows from it. In the Torah's logic, delaying a vow causes the four evil traits; annulling vows reverses that causation. This node is the hinge of the entire teaching.

nodes.role_in_package: The spiritual mechanism — meriting the annulment of vows

new_packages.name_en: Annulment of the Four Evil Traits
new_packages.rationale: Both nodes share the same essential nature: the nullification of or salvation from the four cardinal sins (idolatry, sexual immorality, bloodshed, evil speech). Node 2 frames this as an active annulment (mevatel) and node 5 as passive salvation (nitzoolin). They describe the same outcome — the defeat of these four evils — from two perspectives. The polarity is 'good' because both describe the positive result of overcoming evil, not the evil itself.
